Chapter 5: Making the Greatest Contribution and Building Productive Relationships.
Now that you’ve got a solid grasp of your strengths, work style, and values, it’s time to put all that insight to work—by making the biggest impact you can.
See, it’s not just about chasing your own goals. The real magic happens when you look for the intersection between what’s needed around you, and what only you can offer.
That’s where you get to step up, take ownership, and really deliver results that matter.
So, where do you start?
First, pay close attention to what your organization or community actually needs. What challenges keep popping up? Where are the gaps or opportunities?
When you understand what matters most, you can spot the places where your personal strengths will make the biggest difference.
Here are a few ways to identify those opportunities:
Notice where problems seem stuck, even after lots of effort.
Look for areas where certain skills or viewpoints are missing.
And think about how your own unique experiences—maybe a fresh perspective or a bit of hard-earned knowledge—could help fill those unmet needs.
Once you’ve zeroed in on where you can contribute, it’s important to talk about it.
Share your intentions, ask for feedback, and make sure you’re in sync with the bigger picture.
This not only helps your efforts get noticed, but also opens the door to learning from others and building real connections.
Speaking of connections, productive relationships are absolutely essential if you want to make a lasting impact.
Let’s be real—no one achieves big things alone.
Success almost always comes down to how well you can work with other people.
And building those strong relationships?
It’s about more than just liking each other.
You’ll want to really understand what makes your colleagues tick—their strengths, their preferences, even their quirks.
Try adapting the way you communicate or collaborate to match what works best for them.
And don’t be afraid to offer support, or ask for help when you need it.
Everyone has something valuable to bring to the table.
Of course, you won’t always see eye-to-eye with everyone.
People have different values, work styles, and priorities—and that’s okay.
The trick is to stay patient, practice empathy, and look for common ground.
When you focus on shared goals and respect each other’s differences, you’ll find that your team becomes more than just a collection of individuals—it turns into something much greater.
Remember, making a meaningful contribution isn’t just a one-time thing.
It’s an ongoing process.
As things change and new challenges pop up, stay flexible and open to new opportunities.
Make it a habit to check in, reflect, and ask for feedback.
That way, you’ll keep your efforts focused, keep growing, and help your organization succeed—while growing right along with it.
